PASS for the stated finite-product theorem in the declared real-coefficient, finite rational-domain category. The supplied essential dependency chain establishes both directions, actual raw-envelope equality, explicit regularization, and the complete contact integrals. This verdict does not close the original arbitrary-balanced-carrier problem or certify the comparison dossier as an independent theorem.

The intersection reconstruction is valid in every dimension. Saturation passes to the stated quotient lattices; the two-cone index calculation gives the correct primitive normal classes. Formula (F) proves balancing, and the full symmetric expression (S), including its tangential term, proves commutativity. The three refinement cases preserve both balancing and divisor coefficients, including zero coefficients at newly inserted vertices. The split-lattice calculation (P) applies to every intermediate tensor cycle and proves the exhausted-factor rules. Real coefficients are handled directly, without inferring positivity from signed basis expansions.

The elementary supporting arguments establish the required finite polyhedral facts. In (FC1), the active constraints determine the tangent cone independently of the real relative-interior centre. Rational generators of (FC2) give the finite tests (FC3). Segment convexity and grouped initial directions then establish actual PC for remote rational endpoints, real coefficients, real centres, and every permitted structure. The PC-to-PAPC construction tests every nonnegative real local cycle in each positive dimension on ordinary opens. The reverse construction uses rational local rays and never requires inserting an irrational vertex. The active-face rational-box argument (FC6) exactly decomposes the prescribed reference and preserves all strict recession inequalities.

The positive reduction correctly normalizes actual real weights componentwise: rank one identifies the full kernel, forces rational incident ratios, and leaves one positive real scale per connected component. Unbranched components are complete rational affine lines. The resulting scalar multiplies the complete recursive measure once, because each divisor is linear in its initial cycle.

The multivariate cylinder proof retains all necessary data. The recession constraints define precisely the common finite partial-infimum domain D, which is compact. Projected spatial vertices supply all graph subdivisions; the fibre formulas include finite endpoints and every tail. The incidence system includes every bounded edge and cycle. Its maximum closure and compact-box argument establish the greatest assignment. Elimination gives finite concave node assignments with rational dual gradients and real constants.

The reconstruction Q is the true raw envelope. Touching supports of rational slice completions, followed by propagation through the connected graph, bound every competitor at rational points. Rational enclosing simplices and continuity of Q extend that upper bound to all real points without presuming competitor continuity. Applying it to gamma minus ||u|| gives the lower growth bound; Q itself is therefore an admissible competitor.

The rational-domain argument is essential and succeeds. Conditions (15)–(17) describe the entire maximization regions using rational supergradient vertices, rational primitive graph lengths, and rational normal-cone generators. These regions remain rational despite real dual vertices and real function coefficients. Their vertices occur only over graph nodes, so open-edge strata cannot carry top coefficients.

The contact proof covers every possible atom. A lower-dimensional exposed face C_x gives common nonzero rational lineality after affine subtraction. A full-dimensional C_x gives a strict node cap at interior covectors when contact fails. Raising that single incidence coordinate forces its Laplacian to vanish. Positivity of the weights and concavity make every outgoing slope affine on C_x. The sole star relation then supplies A and the rational map B in (26). After affine subtraction, the germ factors through an m-dimensional complete rational fan. The quotient-vanishing induction removes successive quotient-face codimensions and kills the entire (m+1)-stage coefficient. Both vanishing lemmas are justified under their stated antecedents, and those antecedents are established at their applications.

For higher-relation failure, the rational extreme relation has proper support because the actual weight vector is strictly positive and the kernel has dimension at least two. The intrinsic cap satisfies every relation-cone test, and grouped projections establish PC on the full product. Localization through the exact reference decomposition gives a rational-domain PAPC function equal to the original reference outside a compact set. The supported PCC pins every relevant rational apex-fibre point; interpolation pins the remaining rational bump points. Same-face rational boxes extend this to real centres. Thus the asserted global raw-envelope equality follows. Formula (A2) lists the complete intermediate cycles, retains all d! distinct-factor orders, and gives the coefficient in (H).

For two-branch failure, the tripod assignments annihilate the entire factor kernels and therefore extend to rational ambient maps. The coefficients in (Q) sum to one and cancel both projected displacements. Their fibrewise use pins the whole bad-pair apex fibre. Radial interpolation stays within the homogeneous enclosure and an H-affine coface, and the real-centre extension again uses genuine rational-endpoint PCCs. The original-lattice calculation retains the primitive kink vectors, both cone indices, and the tangential axis corrections. Its axis weights are nonnegative; all kink values vanish in the second divisor; the complete second coefficient is 8ab. Formula (A3) retains every intermediate tensor cycle and surviving order, producing the factor d!/2! and exactly (T).

Both negative integrals are complete evaluations. The homogeneous enclosure has only the origin as an old zero-face where the bump is positive. Every other old atom has zero gap. Refinement for the obstacle introduces no new top coefficient. The resulting measures are finite PA zero-cycles, and P+1/n has exactly the same complete measure for every n. Hence there is no diffuse, escaping, boundary, or infinity contribution. The bounded-shift mass identity (M) is independently justified by mixed commutativity and cancellation of bounded-edge slopes.

I authenticated the cited PDF versions and selected proof endings in [BMPS v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1) and [Allermann–Rau v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0709.3705v3). Their literal coefficient conventions are distinguished correctly from the reconstructed real extension. BMPS uses rational cycle weights, integral slopes and rational constants; its PCCs have rational endpoints and real coefficients. Its PA measure uses the full recursive product without division by d!. Allermann–Rau uses integral cycle weights and integral slopes. Neither the shortened printed commutativity ending nor source continuity assertions are needed for this proof.

Harmless editorial corrections: inherited cylinder labels (1), (2), (3), and (5) should be explicitly linked to the sole rank-one relation, (C), (E), and (D); the final bad-pair reference to (35) should point to the germ (J), with epsilon identified as kappa. These corrections require no mathematical repair. The essential proof is self-contained, so there are no external theorem premises to list.
